originality.rationale: The primary 2026 proof yields one representation for one eligible odd-prime parameter, not a polynomial lower bound on the number of distinct representations for each odd n. The new prime-support collision bound upgrades simultaneous Linnik constructions into a pointwise multiplicity theorem; 2023 Conjecture 4.20 remained a conjecture in the inspected primary text. Actual targeted semantic and textual searches yielded no stronger covering theorem. Implicit prior derivation remains an explicit residual risk.
residual_risks: The relatively short amplification could have been implicit but unstated in older, not fully searchable work.
The original Xylouris dissertation was not read in full; exponent 5 was checked in a modern reference guide citing a 2024 primary mathematical paper.
This does not verify or settle the finitely many low-n cases in the 2023 exact conjecture.

value.rationale: Every sufficiently large odd n is shown to have polynomially many distinct prime+Zumkeller representations, a pointwise result strictly stronger in parity coverage than Li 2026 density bounds and materially addressing the 2023 Somu–Kukla–Tran conjecture. The dyadic simultaneous-parameter method and bounded prime-support overlap give a natural quantitative structural advance; exact small threshold and optimal exponent remain open.
